_readme: ONE FILE PER TRIP. Everything a trip needs: manifest, locations, itineraries. All asset paths are relative to this file's folder. See TRIP_SCHEMA.md for the authoring contract — note that the live contract is scripts/validate-trip.mjs, which is ahead of the doc (pitch, artDirection.fonts, budget.levers).
title: Australia & New Zealand
subtitle: New Year on the harbour, then the Southern Alps

route._legsNote: How each segment of route.svg was travelled. `mode` is one of the Figma 'transport' component set (plane | car | bus | train, node 170:2458) and decides two things: the glyph, and the colour the leg turns once you've passed it — a flight yellows in, anything on the ground greens. Untravelled, every leg is the black line Figma draws. `badge` puts the 22px disc at the leg's midpoint; Figma only marks the flight (node 169:1655), so route-2 declares its mode for the colour without one. A bare string is shorthand for {mode, badge:true}. See Timeline.buildRoute().

map._canvasNote: map.png exported from Figma node 157:3380 — the same artwork as before (127:483) re-exported with more surrounding canvas/margin, which was making the map feel cropped at the edges. The two are pixel-for-pixel identical, just translated and on a bigger canvas (2238x1545 vs 1440x1351). All coordinates below (and the route overlay's x/y/w/h) were recomputed from that exact translation, not re-eyeballed. contentSize/contentOffset are the VISIBLE WINDOW onto that canvas: the 1908x1120 soft-edged box every desktop frame in Figma's Mediaqueries section now masks the artwork with (nodes 176:2921/2925/2929 and 173:2864), sitting at base-image (165.44, 155). Figma places it identically in all four — 674px right and 160px down inside the placed image rect at 1200, 1440, 2156 and 3820 alike — so one window serves the whole desktop ladder and only the viewport around it changes. contentOffset.x + contentSize.w/2 = 1119.44 is therefore still the anchor: the one point of the image that lands on the viewport's centre line at every width, which is what keeps the crop symmetric instead of scaling to fit. contentOffset.y positions the window vertically the same way — see MapView.applyMapMetrics(). narrowScale is how wide the artwork is drawn in the 375 frame (1180px of 2238 = 0.52725); mobile drops the window entirely and shows the whole image, 1:1 at 768 and interpolating below.
map._calibrationNote: All 11 locations (base stops and day-trip spurs alike) are exact — derived by translating the previous exact calibration onto the new, less-cropped map.png (see _canvasNote), then visually verified against the new artwork. Byron Bay, Nimbin and the Gold Coast were added later and placed from the ARTWORK's own geography rather than by eye: the landmass bounding box in map.png gives Cape York, Wilsons Promontory, Steep Point and Cape Byron, and those four real extremes fix a lat/lon scale across 28 degrees. Cross-checked two ways — the easternmost land pixel in the image (Cape Byron is the mainland's most easterly point) lands within 2px of what that scale predicts for Byron Bay.

fonts._readme: Sunshine Formula (script) and Scribble Note (hand) are the real licensed faces, self-hosted under fonts/. Elms Sans (heavy) is still a licensed marketplace font not yet purchased — Nunito stands in for that role until it arrives; only that one entry changes when it does.

hero._stickerNote: Positions are the CENTRE of each sticker, in the centred design canvas's own coordinates (1440 wide / 375 on the mobile canvas) — read from Figma nodes 169:1870 and 169:2355. `w` is the UNROTATED width; `rotate` is applied about that centre, so the rendered bounding box matches the mockup's. `anchor` names the element the y is measured from (its top); without one, y is from the top of the page. Anchoring is what keeps the lower three from drifting when a trip has more budget rows than the mockup did. A sticker with no `narrow` block is simply not drawn on the mobile canvas — Figma's 375 frame drops the kangaroo.

grid._source: Read from the 'Mockup v2' frame's own Figma layout grid (Plugin API node.layoutGrids), not eyeballed: pattern COLUMNS, count 12, gutterSize 20, alignment STRETCH, offset 120, on a 1440-wide frame. This is the unified grid for the whole page — see src/styles/tokens.css (--grid-margin etc.) and grid.css (.grid-12).

locations.subtitle: Circular Quay · Bondi · Manly
locations.intro: We land two days before the year turns and don't move again for over a week. The harbour does most of the work — ferries as public transport, a coastal path that needs no planning, and on the 31st the loudest new year on the planet going off directly overhead.

thingsToDo.title: NYE fireworks from a public harbour vantage point
thingsToDo.note: Free from the public foreshore — Mrs Macquarie's Point, Blues Point, Barangaroo. Free spots ballot or queue from early morning; paid vantage tickets and harbourview dinners are extra and aren't counted here.

thingsToDo.title: Circular Quay and the Opera House at sunset
thingsToDo.note: Arrival-evening walk. Nothing booked, nothing paid.

thingsToDo.title: Bondi to Coogee coastal walk
thingsToDo.note: Self-guided, flat, 2-3 hours. Best done on the 1st when the whole city is moving slowly.

thingsToDo.title: Manly ferry return and a beach afternoon
thingsToDo.note: Opal card fare both ways. The cheapest harbour cruise in Sydney is the scheduled ferry.

thingsToDo.title: Public transport (Opal card)
thingsToDo.note: Trains, buses and the harbour ferries on one card, fare-capped daily and weekly. Priced for a week in the city — it was labelled "~8 jours", which was true of one itinerary and wrong on the other two, and was the only French title in a list of English ones.

thingsToDo.title: Royal Botanic Garden and Mrs Macquarie's Chair
thingsToDo.note: Free. Also the NYE recon walk — you can see exactly where you'd want to stand.

stays.name: Adina Apartment Hotel Sydney Darling Harbour

locations._staysNote: Prices are the PER-PERSON share of a room split three ways, which is how the budget model reads them. Apartment-style beats hotel rooms here — three people in one Adina apartment is cheaper per head than three hotel beds. Book by mid-November: the NYE week is the highest-demand accommodation window of the Australian year.
locations.foodNotes: No pork — easy here. Seafood, Thai and Vietnamese are everywhere; the thing to watch is bacon defaulting into breakfasts.

locations.subtitle: Katoomba · Three Sisters · Scenic World
locations.intro: Two hours west of the harbour and a thousand metres up, into eucalyptus haze and sandstone cliffs. We go as a day trip rather than a stay — the drama is all in the first look over Jamison Valley, and you get that in an afternoon.

thingsToDo.title: Day tour from Sydney — Scenic World, Echo Point and the Three Sisters
thingsToDo.note: Peak-season pricing with hotel pickup, which is also the transport for the day. NSW's bushfire danger period covers these dates — keep the day movable and check the RFS conditions that morning.

thingsToDo.title: Prince Henry Cliff Walk
thingsToDo.note: Free clifftop path between the lookouts. The tour leaves enough time for the Echo Point stretch.

locations._staysNote: Listed for completeness — this is a day trip in both itineraries, so these cost nothing in the budget. They're here in case the Blue Mountains ever get promoted to an overnight.

locations.subtitle: Pokolbin · Semillon · vineyards
locations.intro: Australia's oldest wine region, and the one that makes a white nobody else makes — Hunter Semillon, picked early and left alone for a decade. A slow day of tastings between the Blue Mountains and the coast.

thingsToDo.title: Small-group winery day tour from Sydney
thingsToDo.note: Four to five cellar doors with lunch, and nobody has to drive. Transport for the day is inside this price.

thingsToDo.title: Hot air balloon over the vineyards at dawn
thingsToDo.note: About an hour aloft at sunrise, then breakfast. The single most expensive thing anyone does on this trip — it was priced at zero here, which is what a free walk costs, not a balloon.

locations.subtitle: Nelson Bay · Stockton dunes · dolphins
locations.intro: White sand, a bay with about a hundred resident bottlenose dolphins, and the largest moving coastal sand mass in the southern hemisphere to throw ourselves down. Jervis Bay south of Sydney is the alternative — same idea, whiter sand, longer drive.

thingsToDo.title: Dolphin watching cruise, Nelson Bay
thingsToDo.note: About 90 minutes. Runs Nov-Apr only, so these dates are dead centre of the season and sightings are near-guaranteed.

thingsToDo.title: Sandboarding and 4WD tour, Stockton Sand Dunes
thingsToDo.note: Thirty-two kilometres of dune. Go early — the sand is genuinely too hot to walk on by midday in January.

stays.name: Oaks Port Stephens Pacific Blue Resort

locations._staysNote: A day trip in the 20-day plan and a five-night base in the coach plan, which is why the stays are priced properly rather than left as placeholders.

locations.subtitle: Lake Wakatipu · Gibbston · Arrowtown
locations.intro: The pivot of the trip: we swap a city of five million for a town of fifteen thousand with mountains on every side. Everything worth doing on this half of the island starts here, and for the first five nights we do it without a car.

thingsToDo.title: Skyline Gondola at sunset
thingsToDo.note: Return gondola. Go up for the last light over Wakatipu, not for the restaurant.

thingsToDo.title: Kawarau Bridge bungy
thingsToDo.note: The original, 43 metres, since 1988. Shotover Jet costs roughly the same if the jet boat appeals more than the fall — budget for one, not both.

thingsToDo.title: Ben Lomond Track
thingsToDo.note: Free, six to eight hours return from town, 1,438m at the top. The hard day of the trip.

thingsToDo.title: TSS Earnslaw lake cruise
thingsToDo.note: Coal-fired steamer from 1912, still running on its original boilers.

thingsToDo.title: Gibbston Valley wine tasting
thingsToDo.note: Central Otago pinot noir, twenty minutes out of town, past the bungy bridge.

thingsToDo.title: Arrowtown and the Chinese settlement
thingsToDo.note: Gold-rush village, free to wander. Bring money for lunch, not for entry.

thingsToDo.title: Glenorchy and the Paradise valley road
thingsToDo.note: Forty-five minutes of lake road, and the Routeburn trailhead at the end of it if there's appetite for a day walk.

locations._staysNote: January averages around NZD 255 a night for a mid-range room here — expensive, but nothing like the NYE spike we've already paid for in Sydney.
locations.foodNotes: No pork. Lamb, venison and green-lipped mussels are the local defaults, so this is the easy half of the trip.

locations.subtitle: Te Anau · Homer Tunnel · Mitre Peak
locations.intro: A long day and the only unavoidable one — four to five hours of coach each way through Te Anau and the Homer Tunnel, for two hours on the water under a mountain that comes straight out of it. January is Fiordland's wettest month, which is the good news: the waterfalls only exist when it rains.

thingsToDo.title: Milford Sound coach and cruise day trip from Queenstown
thingsToDo.note: Full day, roughly 5am to 8pm. Coach beats self-driving: the road is spectacular and you can't look at it while driving it. Cruises sail in any weather.

thingsToDo.title: Mirror Lakes and The Chasm roadside stops
thingsToDo.note: Included in the coach day. Free, brief, and worth getting off the bus for.

stays.name: Te Anau Lakeview Kiwi Holiday Park & Motels
Distinction Luxmore Hotel Lake Te Anau

locations._staysNote: Te Anau stays, listed in case the day trip ever becomes an overnight. As a spur they cost nothing in the budget.

locations.subtitle: Manapouri · Wilmot Pass · overnight
locations.intro: Milford's quieter, larger neighbour — a hundred visitors a day against Milford's thousand, reached by boat and then over a mountain pass by coach. You sleep on the water, and at some point the crew cut the engines and let it go completely silent.

thingsToDo.title: Doubtful Sound overnight cruise
thingsToDo.note: Sails mid-afternoon, sleeps aboard in the fiord, back the next afternoon. Counted as a day trip out of Queenstown and priced with the bed included — so the Queenstown night it overlaps is paid twice, once here and once in the hotel line. Left as-is deliberately: most people keep the room rather than pack it up for one night.

locations._staysNote: You sleep on the boat, not in these — they exist because the schema wants three stays per location and because a night ashore in Manapouri is the fallback if the cruise is cancelled.

locations.subtitle: Roys Peak · Rob Roy · that tree
locations.intro: An hour over the Crown Range from Queenstown and about a tenth of the noise. This is where we pick up the car and stop being on anyone else's schedule — two nights, one big climb, and a willow standing in the lake that half the internet has already photographed.

thingsToDo.title: Roys Peak Track
thingsToDo.note: Free. Five to six hours return, 1,200m of climb, and the view everyone comes for is 45 minutes before the summit. Start before 6am to beat both the heat and the queue at the viewpoint.

thingsToDo.title: Rob Roy Glacier Track
thingsToDo.note: Free, three to four hours, gentler than Roys. The access road crosses unbridged fords — check the rental agreement covers it before committing.

thingsToDo.title: That Wanaka Tree at first light
thingsToDo.note: Five minutes from town. Ten minutes of your life. Go at dawn or don't bother.

thingsToDo.title: Puzzling World
thingsToDo.note: Illusion rooms and a large outdoor maze. Deeply silly and the right thing to do on a rest afternoon.

locations.subtitle: Lindis Pass · Good Shepherd · dark sky
locations.intro: Three hours from Wanaka over the Lindis Pass, into a lake the colour of glacier flour and a village that switched off its streetlights on purpose. It sits inside an international dark sky reserve, which is the entire reason to sleep here rather than pass through.

thingsToDo.title: Church of the Good Shepherd
thingsToDo.note: Free, tiny, and photographed from every angle already. Worth five minutes at either end of the day, not at noon.

thingsToDo.title: Tekapo Springs hot pools
thingsToDo.note: The right thing to do after the Lindis Pass drive.

thingsToDo.title: Mt John dark-sky stargazing tour
thingsToDo.note: Guided, telescopes, runs late. Southern Cross and the Magellanic Clouds — neither of which is visible from home. Cancelled if cloudy, so book the first of the two nights and keep the second as backup.

locations.subtitle: Hooker Valley · Tasman Glacier · 3,724m
locations.intro: An hour up the side of Lake Pukaki from Tekapo, dead-ending at the tallest mountain in the country. The best walk here is also the easiest one, which almost never happens — flat, three swing bridges, and a lake with icebergs floating in it at the end.

thingsToDo.title: Hooker Valley Track
thingsToDo.note: Free. Ten kilometres return, three hours, almost no climb, and it ends at Hooker Lake with Aoraki straight ahead. The single best value walk of the trip.

thingsToDo.title: Tasman Glacier viewpoint and terminal lake
thingsToDo.note: Free, forty minutes return on the way back out. New Zealand's longest glacier, retreating fast enough to see the difference decade to decade.

locations._staysNote: A day trip from Tekapo, so these cost nothing. Sleeping in the village is the upgrade if the dark-sky night gets clouded out — Mount Cook is inside the same reserve.

locations.subtitle: Avon · Banks Peninsula · Akaroa
locations.intro: Three and a half hours down from Tekapo and the car goes back. A city still visibly rebuilding itself fifteen years on, a garden you can punt through, and an hour over the hills the world's smallest and rarest dolphin.

thingsToDo.title: International Antarctic Centre
thingsToDo.note: Little blue penguins, huskies, a storm room and a Hägglund ride. Five minutes from the airport, so it doubles as the last morning.

thingsToDo.title: Akaroa harbour cruise, self-drive
thingsToDo.note: Cruise only — we still have the car, so we skip the coach tour and drive the ninety minutes ourselves. Hector's dolphins are endemic to the South Island and this is the reliable place to see them.

thingsToDo.title: Botanic Gardens and punting on the Avon
thingsToDo.note: Half an hour on a flat-bottomed boat with someone else doing the work. Unserious, and exactly right for the last afternoon.

locations.foodNotes: No pork. Riverside Market covers everyone; the thing to check is the Canterbury pub menus, which put bacon in most things.

locations.subtitle: Cape Byron · Main Beach · the hinterland
locations.intro: The deliberate change of gear. Seven days of a city of five million, then a town you can cross on foot in twenty minutes, where the main street runs out at the sand. The mainland’s most easterly point is a half-hour walk from the pub.

thingsToDo.title: Cape Byron lighthouse walk
thingsToDo.note: Free, about 3.7km round the headland from Main Beach. Go at sunrise — it is the first place on the mainland the sun hits, and the dolphins are usually in the bay.

thingsToDo.title: Surf lesson at Main Beach
thingsToDo.note: Two hours, board and wetsuit in. A long, forgiving beach break — this is the place to learn rather than the Gold Coast’s points.

thingsToDo.title: Wategos and The Pass
thingsToDo.note: Free. The two swimming beaches round the headland, both calmer than Main Beach and both a walk rather than a drive.

thingsToDo.title: Crystal Castle botanic gardens
thingsToDo.note: Twenty minutes inland. Worth it for the rainforest walk and the view back over the hinterland.

locations._staysNote: Byron leans casual — beach shacks, eco-stays and guesthouses rather than chains. A shared flat near the centre often beats all three on a three-way split.

locations.subtitle: Rainforest · waterfalls · the hinterland
locations.intro: An hour inland and a long way from the coast in every other sense: a village that never quite left 1973, at the foot of an extinct volcano, surrounded by rainforest and waterfalls.

thingsToDo.title: Nimbin and Minyon Falls day trip
thingsToDo.note: Full day out of Byron. The falls drop 100m into rainforest and are the reason to go; the village is the story you tell afterwards.

locations._staysNote: Listed because every location carries them, not because we are staying — this is a day out of Byron. If it ever became an overnight, the hinterland is where you would sleep, not the village.

locations.subtitle: Burleigh Heads · Surfers Paradise · Currumbin
locations.intro: Byron with the volume up: high-rises straight onto the sand, a theme park every ten minutes, and at Burleigh Heads one of the best right-hand points in the country. The last three days are deliberately easy ones.

thingsToDo.title: Burleigh Heads headland walk
thingsToDo.note: Free, 30 minutes through the national park round the point. Best at the end of the day, watching the surfers on the point below.

thingsToDo.title: Movie World or Dreamworld
thingsToDo.note: One park, one day — they are ten minutes apart and doing both is a waste of a beach. Book online, it is materially cheaper than the gate.

thingsToDo.title: Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary
thingsToDo.note: The one place on this trip to actually see koalas and kangaroos without pretending a zoo is a national park.

thingsToDo.title: SkyPoint at Surfers Paradise
thingsToDo.note: 77 floors up for the length of the coast at sunset. Twenty minutes, then leave.

locations._staysNote: Apartment-style high-rises are the norm here and they split three ways better than anywhere else on the trip — two bedrooms, a kitchen and a pool for the price of two hotel rooms.

itineraries._dayPlanNote: Optional: one entry per day, in order, naming what that day IS. {"at":"blue-mountains"} is a day trip — the card and the map's active pin move to it while the route stays put at the stay it hangs off. {"at":"sydney","place":"Bondi Beach"} keeps you in Sydney but titles the day. `at` takes any locationId, base or day trip; `place` is free text that overrides the name on the card. Omit dayPlan entirely and Timeline.buildSchedule() derives one: each base fills its own nights and its day trips are spread evenly through them, skipping the arrival day — right about where you sleep, a guess about which day each trip falls on. Fill this in to pin that down.
itineraries.label: Harbour & the Southern Alps
itineraries._flightsNote: Two flights inside the trip: into Sydney, and Sydney to Queenstown on 7 Jan. The Christchurch flight home is treated as going home rather than a trip leg — change to 3 if you'd rather count it.
itineraries._datesNote: Nineteen nights on the ground, 30 Dec to 18 Jan. The draft's 'day 20-21, Jan 18-19' is the journey home across the date line, which sits outside the itinerary the way the return flight does.

mood.headline: You arrive at the start of the year, in the middle of summer.
mood.body: Sydney turns the year over before almost anywhere else on earth, in twenty-eight degrees and flip-flops. Two weeks later you're at the foot of a glacier in the same shorts. Same summer, opposite ends of it.

arguments.headline: The fireworks are the opening, not the point.
arguments.body: One and a half million people watch it from the foreshore for nothing, and then the whole city takes a week off. Eight days of harbour, coast and mountains while everyone back home has already gone back to work.

arguments.headline: Halfway through, you stop being on anyone's schedule.
arguments.body: Queenstown to Wanaka to Tekapo to Christchurch, in a car, at whatever pace the road suggests. The second half of this trip has no guide, no pickup time and no group.

arguments.headline: Longest days of the year, and the darkest skies.
arguments.body: Light in Fiordland until close to ten at night, so a serious walk can start after lunch. Then Tekapo, inside an international dark sky reserve, where the village turned its streetlights off on purpose.

gem.headline: You walk to the foot of the highest mountain in the country, on a flat path.
gem.body: Three swing bridges, three hours, almost no climb — and it ends at a lake with icebergs in it, Aoraki filling the whole windscreen of the valley. The best thing in New Zealand costs nothing and doesn't need to be booked.
gem.label: One more thing…

flightSearch._note: An open jaw into Sydney and out of Christchurch, with the trans-Tasman hop in the middle. PAR is the search origin because two of the three of us start there — from Antananarivo it's TNR with a Johannesburg or Nairobi connection, and from Lyon it's LYS or a short hop to CDG. Everyone books their own.

itineraries._dayPlanNote: Optional: one entry per day, in order, naming what that day IS. {"at":"blue-mountains"} is a day trip — the card and the map's active pin move to it while the route stays put at the stay it hangs off. {"at":"sydney","place":"Bondi Beach"} keeps you in Sydney but titles the day. `at` takes any locationId, base or day trip; `place` is free text that overrides the name on the card. Omit dayPlan entirely and Timeline.buildSchedule() derives one: each base fills its own nights and its day trips are spread evenly through them, skipping the arrival day — right about where you sleep, a guess about which day each trip falls on. Fill this in to pin that down.
itineraries.label: No-car version
itineraries._flightsNote: Into Sydney, Sydney to Queenstown on 7 Jan, Queenstown to Christchurch on 14 Jan. The flight home is excluded, same convention as the other two.
itineraries._note: The no-car version, tightened from 21 days to 18: Port Stephens loses two of its five nights and Queenstown one of its eight. Nothing else goes — all four bases, both fiords and every activity are still here, they are just less padded. Queenstown at seven nights still covers Milford, Doubtful and the two free valley days with a spare.

mood.headline: Nobody has to drive.
mood.body: Four bases in three weeks. You unpack, and then everything comes to you — coaches, ferries, boats, a gondola. The only thing you have to be on time for is the boat.

arguments.headline: Four bases, not a suitcase relay.
arguments.body: Sydney, then a bay on the New South Wales coast, then one town in the mountains for over a week. Long enough in each to stop reading maps.

arguments.headline: Doubtful Sound instead of Milford.
arguments.body: A hundred visitors a day against Milford's thousand, and you sleep on the water rather than turning round at the mouth of it.

arguments.headline: The wildlife here isn't a maybe.
arguments.body: About a hundred bottlenose dolphins live in Port Stephens year-round, and Akaroa holds the world's smallest and rarest dolphin. Neither of these is a lottery.

gem.headline: They cut the engines and let the fiord go silent.
gem.body: Somewhere in Doubtful Sound the crew stop the boat, kill the generator and ask everyone not to speak. No engine, no road within fifty kilometres, no phone signal — just water against a rock wall eight hundred metres high.
gem.label: One more thing…

flightSearch._note: Open jaw into Sydney and out of Christchurch, with both internal hops in between. PAR is the search origin because two of the three of us start there — the ledger’s own dropdown is what re-prices the long-haul per person.

itineraries.label: East coast, two bases
itineraries._flightsNote: Two flights inside the trip: into Sydney, and Sydney to Ballina on 6 Jan. The flight home is treated as going home rather than a trip leg, the same convention as the other two.
itineraries._note: The short version, and the cheapest: two bases joined by one 90-minute hop, no trans-Tasman crossing and no rental car to drop in another city. Built to come in under the €3,500 cap.
itineraries._dayPlanNote: One entry per day, in order, naming what that day IS — a day trip moves the card and the active pin to the spur while the route stays put at the base it belongs to.

mood.headline: Two towns, one coast, and nothing in between to organise.
mood.body: Sydney turns the year over in twenty-eight degrees, and a week later you are on a beach six hundred kilometres north where the main street runs out at the sand. One flight joins them. Everything else is walking.

arguments.headline: The whole trip is two check-ins.
arguments.body: Seven nights in Sydney, six on the northern beaches, and a single 90-minute hop between them. No trans-Tasman crossing, no rental car to drop in a different city, no internal leg longer than a lunch.

arguments.headline: It is the version that fits the budget.
arguments.body: One internal flight instead of a multi-leg loop, and the northern beaches run cheaper per night than anywhere in Sydney. This is the shape that comes in under the cap without cutting the New Year.

arguments.headline: You still get the fireworks.
arguments.body: Sydney is the whole point of going at New Year, and this keeps all seven nights of it — the harbour, the coastal walk, the mountains and the wine — before trading the city for the sand.

gem.headline: You can walk to the first place the sun touches the country.
gem.body: Cape Byron is the most easterly point of mainland Australia, and the path to it starts at the end of Byron’s main street — 3.7km round the headland, free, dolphins in the bay below most mornings. Be up for it once and the whole continent gets its light after you do.
gem.label: One more thing…

flightSearch._note: Open jaw into Sydney and out of the Gold Coast, with the Ballina hop in the middle. PAR is the search origin because two of the three of us start there — the ledger’s own dropdown is what re-prices the fare per person.

itineraries._budgetNote: Matches what the ledger itemises for the default departure city (Paris). Lyon adds ~100 and Antananarivo ~100-300 more — the dropdown above the list is what re-prices it.

budget._readme: v2 ledger model (final-call-v1-vs-v2-spec.md §2: 'ledger chronologique poste par poste'). Per person. No levers, no comfort-tier multiplier — src/js/data.js:buildLedger() groups each base stop's hotel (the 'budget'-tier stay × nights) with every thingsToDo entry for it and its spurs, plus any `fixed` line tagged to it via locationId. Food isn't tracked (spec: 'ledger exhaustif, hors nourriture').
budget._fixedNote: Internal flights live on each ITINERARY (itineraries[].fixed), not here: the same city is flown into on one variant and driven to on another, so a trip-level line keyed only by locationId bills a flight nobody takes. See buildLedger().

origins.label: Paris
origins.note: Qantas fly Paris–Sydney direct three times a week, about 22 hours. Peak-season pricing over New Year.

origins.label: Lyon
origins.note: A short hop to Paris and onto the same direct, or one stop with a Gulf carrier. Roughly a hundred euros on top of the Paris fare.

origins.label: Antananarivo
origins.note: No direct route — two stops via Johannesburg or Nairobi, 20 to 25 hours. January is the priciest month on this one, so book early.

budget._originsNote: The three of us leave from three different cities, so the long-haul fare is the one line in the ledger that depends on WHO is reading it. The dropdown above the list picks between them and the flight line re-prices; everything else is shared and identical. Ranges are peak-season (Dec/Jan) return economy estimates, not quotes — they are the least certain numbers on the page. originLocationId is the stop the line is filed under, i.e. the one you fly into.

flightSearch._legsNote: Legs live on each itinerary, because the middle hop moves with the duration. Three of us travelling, but from three different cities — the search is priced from Paris and everyone books their own ticket.
flightSearch._bookingNote: Lock the long-haul first. Sydney at New Year and the South Island in January are the two most in-demand windows either country has.
